question: Which venomous snake is most commonly linked to severe snakebites on farms in Nigeria?
explanation: The West African carpet viper lives in agricultural fields and causes the majority of venomous bites in Nigerian farming communities. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T7#BMP110_U7_T7_h1)

question: Why do rural Nigerian midwives often need to manage animal bites and stings?

options.A: They are frequently the primary healthcare providers available in rural communities.
options.B: Government policy requires midwives to handle all veterinary emergencies.
options.C: Snakes and insects only attack pregnant women in rural areas.
options.D: Traditional healers refuse to treat any form of animal injury.

explanation: Because primary health centers are often understaffed, midwives frequently provide the first emergency care for bite and sting patients. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T7#BMP110_U7_T7_h1)

question: What is the very first step when arriving at the scene of a reported animal bite?

options.B: Ensuring the environment is safe for the rescuer
options.C: Washing the bite wound with clean water
options.D: Applying a tight tourniquet above the wound

explanation: A rescuer must stay safe to avoid becoming another patient; scene safety always comes before patient care. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T7#BMP110_U7_T7_h2)

question: Relatives bring a dead snake to the clinic along with a snakebite patient. What should you do?

options.A: Throw the snake away immediately without looking at it.
options.B: Use the dead snake to demonstrate first aid techniques to the patient.
options.C: Warn everyone not to touch the head because reflex bites can still inject venom.
options.D: Examine the fangs closely with your bare hands to identify the species.

explanation: Even after a snake is dead, nerve reflexes can cause it to bite and release venom if handled carelessly. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T7#BMP110_U7_T7_h2)

question: Why should you scrape out a bee stinger with a flat card instead of pulling it with tweezers?

options.A: Tweezers can squeeze the attached venom sac and inject more poison.
options.B: Scraping removes the entire underlying sweat gland safely.
options.C: Scraping is the only way to kill the remaining bacteria on the skin.
options.D: Tweezers will permanently stain the skin around the sting site.

explanation: Pinching the venom sac with tweezers pushes more toxin into the skin, making the reaction worse. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T7#BMP110_U7_T7_h3)

question: How should a snake-bitten limb be positioned while transporting the patient to the clinic?

options.A: Elevated high above the chest level
options.C: Immobilized at the level of the heart
options.D: Immersed in a bucket of ice water

explanation: Keeping the limb at heart level slows down how fast the venom spreads through the body while keeping blood flowing properly. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T7#BMP110_U7_T7_h3)

question: Which medication is the main emergency treatment for severe allergic reactions like anaphylaxis?
explanation: Adrenaline quickly opens up the airways, reduces swelling, and helps maintain blood pressure during a severe allergic reaction. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T7#BMP110_U7_T7_h4)

question: A patient stung by a wasp 10 minutes ago develops noisy breathing, swollen lips, and dizziness. What is happening?
explanation: Trouble breathing and swelling in the face combined with dizziness are classic signs of a dangerous systemic allergic reaction. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T7#BMP110_U7_T7_h4)

question: What is a major medical risk of tying a tight tourniquet after a snakebite?

options.A: Tissue death and possible gangrene of the limb
options.B: Immediate neutralization of all snake venom
options.C: Complete prevention of local skin swelling
options.D: Rapid acceleration of normal blood clotting

explanation: Stopping blood flow completely starves the tissues of oxygen, which can destroy the limb and lead to amputation. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T7#BMP110_U7_T7_h5)

question: Why should healthcare workers advise people not to make cuts on a snakebite wound?

options.A: It neutralizes the effectiveness of future antivenom doses.
options.B: It makes it impossible to identify the snake species later.
options.C: It causes the venom to travel faster through bone marrow.
options.D: It introduces severe infection and increases dangerous bleeding.

explanation: Cutting the skin damages blood vessels and tissues, which worsens bleeding and lets germs into the wound. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T7#BMP110_U7_T7_h5)

question: Which sign shows that a snakebite is affecting the whole body and needs urgent antivenom?

options.A: Mild itching localized strictly around the small bite mark
options.B: Anxiety and fear experienced immediately after the bite
options.C: Spontaneous bleeding from the gums or puncture sites
options.D: A slight redness measuring less than two centimeters

explanation: Bleeding in areas away from the bite means the venom is affecting the blood clotting system throughout the entire body. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T7#BMP110_U7_T7_h6)

question: Why must antivenom be given in a clinic or hospital equipped to handle severe reactions?

options.A: The medication must be boiled before entering the bloodstream.
options.B: Antivenom itself can trigger severe allergic reactions or anaphylaxis.
options.C: Hospital staff are the only people legally allowed to open the vial.
options.D: Patients always lose consciousness immediately upon receiving the injection.

explanation: Because antivenom is made from animal proteins, it can sometimes cause a severe allergic reaction that needs quick medical treatment. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T7#BMP110_U7_T7_h6)

question: What environmental action helps prevent snakes from hiding near rural homes?

options.A: Planting dense flowering shrubs near the main entrance
options.B: Clearing tall grass and bushes close to dwellings
options.C: Keeping windows wide open without mosquito nets
options.D: Leaving firewood stacked neatly right against bedroom walls

explanation: Clearing away thick vegetation removes the hiding spots and hunting grounds that attract snakes to living areas. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T7#BMP110_U7_T7_h7)

question: During an antenatal health talk, what practical footwear advice should a midwife give pregnant farmers?

options.A: Wear sturdy boots and protective trousers when working on the farm.
options.B: Walk barefoot to feel the soil texture and avoid slipping.
options.C: Wear open sandals to keep the feet cool during hot farm work.
options.D: Wrap thin cotton cloth around bare feet for protection.

explanation: Thick boots and trousers act as a physical barrier to protect the skin if someone accidentally steps near a camouflaged snake. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T7#BMP110_U7_T7_h7)
